transcript:
Header:
Date: 2026-05-22 10:00 AM PT
Duration: ~60 minutes
Attendees: Maya Patel (Redwood AE), Diego Ramos (Redwood SE), Sarah Nguyen (Bluecrest SRE), Tom Brant (Bluecrest CTO), Priya Singh (Bluecrest Platform)

Summary (auto): quick review of yesterday's afternoon load where we saw a surgeback event, discuss root causes and immediate mitigations, agree on canary and runbook handover.

[00:00] Maya (AE): Hey everyone, thanks for joining. quick check—can you hear me ok?
[00:05] Sarah: Yeah loud and clear. Side note, running on a weird hotspot here in prod-sim but fine.
[00:12] Maya: Cool. Agenda—diego will run through traces from yesterday's 3pm test, then we discuss telemetry gaps and a plan for a 2-hour canary with egress shaping and quant.
[00:22] Diego (SE): Alright, I'll jump in. So I pulled the flame graphs and tail latencies. The spike—i'm calling it "surgeback"—happened around minute 28 of the load when sequence lengths trended up. We see KV cache churn, and a bunch of small kernel OOM retries on the shard that had older driver.
[00:38] Priya: When you say "older driver" you mean the CUDA runtime on that node?
[00:43] Diego: yeah, some nodes on the private pool were still on 545.x while the rest are on 550.x, and the kernel scheduling interactions look bad under the longer-context workload.
[00:51] Tom: so it's a kernel thing, not a network egress problem? we saw increased egress but that might be a symptom.
[00:58] Diego: correct, it's multi-factor. network queuing increased due to longer responses, which fed back into batch sizing, and then the cache thrash made per-token op cost jump.
[01:12] Sarah: there's also a couple of missing traces in our Datadog - some spans are gone for the 3pm window, which is why our alerting didn't kick until the app team manual check.
[01:22] Maya: ok that's telemetry gap—probably agent side sampling during high load. we'll cover runbook items.
[01:27] Diego: i have a snippet here—(link posted in chat) trace id abc123-ish—shows prefix KV evictions. the runtime log shows quant fallback in a few cases. i think when the kernel version is mismatched it falls back to a slower exec path and that increases latency.
[01:45] Priya: we're running a custom quant profile for save/cost. could that be exacerbating the fallbacks?
[01:52] Diego: possibly. if fallback gets triggered it disables some optimized kernels. for the canary i'd like to try the conservative quant profile we recommended and also pin the kernel to the newer version.
[02:05] Tom: what's the risk of pinning kernel? downtime?
[02:09] Diego: it requires a rolling restart of the pool. in the worst case you'd have a brief window where some requests go to fallback capacity. we can do it in a maintenance window.
[02:18] Sarah: we prefer late-night UTC windows. Tom, any objections?
[02:22] Tom: no objections, late-night works. but i'd like to try the canary without rolling patch first. if the canary still reproduces the surgeback then we commit to rollback + patch.
[02:33] Maya: that's fair. so plan A: run 2-hour canary with egress shaping + conservative quant, no kernel change. Plan B: if surgeback reproduces, schedule kernel rollback window.
[02:45] Priya: on egress shaping—what are the params? i saw mention of a 20% cap on concurrent outbound per-host?
[02:52] Diego: yeah we suggested soft cap 20-30% and burst allowances for retries. it's mostly to avoid single-host egress saturation that causes queuing upstream.
[03:02] Sarah: also want better alerting—we have a metric threshold but it didn't catch the pattern because we alert on 99th p50 not the rising variance.
[03:12] Maya: we should add an alert on delta of 95/50 ratio and also an increase in eviction rate for the KV namespace.
[03:20] Tom: how long to instrument that?
[03:22] Diego: we can push a quick agent patch to add eviction-rate metric within a day, and dashboards in a few hours using the existing logs.
[03:30] Priya: are we comfortable with the data residency/egress compliance impact when we enable egress shaping? bluecrest needs to ensure logs remain within the private VPC.
[03:39] Maya: shaping doesn't change egress destination, it just controls burst. logs remain inside the VPC, nothing crosses to public endpoints.
[03:46] Sarah: ok good.
[03:48] Diego: one more finding—the request fanout for certain product verticals is high due to an internal router mis-tagging chunked requests, so effective sequence length spikes. we patched router mapping but want to watch in canary.
[04:03] Tom: that mapping patch—when did you deploy?
[04:06] Diego: last night at 22:40 UTC, non-disruptive. initial sampling showed reduced average length but outliers remain.
[04:15] Maya: thank you for the context. let's talk actions and timeline. Diego—can you run that 2-hour canary with these changes: conservative quant profile, egress shaping 25%, no kernel update, and send results?
[04:28] Diego: yep i'll schedule it for Friday 02:00 UTC when bluecrest prefers late-night. i'll run a 2-hour run starting 02:00 with detailed traces and post the spreadsheet.
[04:36] Tom: friday is fine. we need to be able to abort quickly if retries explode.
[04:41] Diego: agreed, abort threshold set at 5x normal 95th percentile and eviction-rates above threshold.
[04:48] Sarah: i want a pre-check the hour before to confirm sampling is good—last time sampling dropped.
[04:53] Maya: we'll do a 30-minute pre-check and i will share a checklist.
[04:58] Priya: on the kernel rollback question—what's the rollback plan exactly?
[05:03] Diego: it's a targeted rollback of the runtime kernel package on the affected pool nodes to 545.x stable build that we tested, done one shard at a time with healthchecks. total time ~2 hours including verification.
[05:15] Tom: that's the fallback plan if canary reproduces surgeback. what's probability you think?
[05:19] Diego: 40-60% if outliers keep spiking. it's sensitive to sequence-length distribution.
[05:25] Maya: ok. other topics—telemetry runbook. i drafted a runbook that covers detecting surgeback, immediate mitigations, and postmortem steps. i'll share after this call.
[05:36] Sarah: would like an explicit section for SSO/portal escalation so our on-call knows who to call.
[05:41] Maya: added. also added a step for exporting traces to the secure S3 bucket and redaction notes for PHI.
[05:49] Priya: good. Bluecrest has strict policies about trace retention—how long will Redwood keep samples?
[05:55] Maya: by default 7 days on this pilot, we can increase retention for the canary window upon request and then delete. i'll put that in the runbook.
[06:05] Tom: any concern about competitor approaches—Anthropic had a recent paper on adaptive batching—could that help avoiding surgeback?
[06:13] Diego: adaptive batching helps but only if you can bound sequence-length variance upstream. our immediate levers are egress shaping and quant conservative profile. adaptive batching is medium-term.
[06:24] Sarah: ok. scheduling and handoffs—Maya will share runbook by 5/23, diego runs canary 5/25 02:00 UTC (2h), post results same day.
[06:35] Priya: i'll monitor logs and forward to infra.
[06:38] Maya: last bit—we should run a short kernel compatibility smoke after the canary if we plan to roll. if canary is clean we can still patch in staged way.
[06:48] Tom: agreed. if the canary is clean, we want a staged patch pushing out over two days to reduce blast radius.
[06:55] Maya: great. Questions?
[07:00] Sarah: none right now. thanks.
[07:03] Maya: okay final recap — three actions: telemetry runbook, 2h canary, confirm rollback window. we'll meet next Tuesday same time for results readout. thanks everyone.

Notes on transcription: Some proper nouns may be off (trace ids, exact kernel versions), occasional filler and overlap. Links shared in chat: /shared/bluecrest/pilot-canary-results.xlsx, /docs/redwood/private-runbook-v2.md

End of transcript.
